objectives.statement: Identify EF Core as a lightweight, extensible, open-source, cross-platform object-relational mapper for working with databases through .NET objects.
Explain that an EF Core model consists of entity classes and a context object representing a session with the database.
Explain that a DbContext is normally a short-lived unit of work whose lifetime ends when the instance is disposed.
Identify EF Core migrations as incremental updates that keep a database schema synchronized with a changing model while preserving existing data.
Distinguish conventions, data annotations, and the Fluent API as ways to configure and customize the EF Core model.
Explain that exposing a type through a DbSet property includes it in the EF Core model as an entity type.
Explain that EF Core uses strongly typed LINQ queries which a database provider translates into database-specific query language.
Identify tracking as the default behavior for queries that return entity types and explain its relationship to SaveChanges.
Distinguish no-tracking queries as suitable for read-only scenarios because returned entities are not kept in the change tracker.
Explain how change tracking and SaveChanges persist detected additions, modifications, and deletions.
Identify the principal EF Core entity states such as Detached, Unchanged, Added, Deleted, and Modified.
Distinguish common methods that cause entities to become tracked, including Add, Attach, and Update.
Explain that ASP.NET Core dependency injection can manage DbContext instances with a request-oriented lifetime through AddDbContext.
objectives.citation: DbContext in dependency injection for ASP.NET Core

objectives.statement: Diagnose concurrent use of a single DbContext instance as an invalid threading pattern and explain why asynchronous operations must be awaited before reuse.
Explain how EF Core compares a current model with a previous model snapshot to generate migration source files when the model evolves.
Distinguish ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete as direct bulk database operations from the change-tracking SaveChanges approach.
Explain that relationships in EF Core connect entity types through foreign keys and navigation properties in the model.
Explain identity resolution as returning the same entity instance for repeated occurrences of the same entity in a query result when the behavior is enabled.
Identify EF Core Package Manager Console and .NET CLI tools as design-time tools used for migrations and reverse engineering.
Diagnose failing to await an asynchronous EF Core operation before starting another operation on the same context as a source of concurrency errors.
Identify the supported model-development approaches of generating a model from an existing database, hand-coding it, or using a visual designer.
Explain that the EF Core context object provides the entry point for querying and saving entity data.
Identify a DbContext as a session-like object that coordinates entity access to a database.
Distinguish database schema evolution from ordinary data querying in the purpose of EF Core migrations.
Explain that model configuration can be grouped into separate configuration classes and applied through the model-building process.
Identify OnModelCreating and ModelBuilder as the Fluent API surface for customizing an EF Core model.
objectives.citation: Use fluent API to configure a model

objectives.statement: Explain that data annotations are attributes used to configure aspects of entity types and their properties.
objectives.citation: Use data annotations to configure a model

objectives.statement: Identify conventions as heuristics that infer common model configuration patterns.
Explain that an entity type exposed by a DbSet property is normally included in the model by convention.
Distinguish excluding a type from the EF Core model from merely excluding it from migrations.
Identify a database provider as the component that translates EF Core query representations into a database-specific language.
Explain that LINQ queries can use a derived context and entity classes to reference database objects through .NET types.
Identify loading all entities, loading one entity, and filtering as common EF Core querying operations.
Explain that a query can be filtered with a LINQ predicate before its results are materialized.
Distinguish a query that returns entity types from a custom projection when considering tracking behavior.
Explain that tracking behavior controls whether EF Core keeps information about an entity instance in its change tracker.
Identify tracking queries as the default for queries returning entity types with defined keys.
Explain that AsNoTracking requests a query whose entity results are not tracked by the context.
Distinguish no-tracking identity resolution as a mode that can reuse entity instances without making the results tracked by the context.
Explain that keyless entity types are never tracked by EF Core.
Identify the change tracker as the mechanism that records entity changes for persistence by SaveChanges.
Explain that a tracked entity can move among Detached, Unchanged, Added, Deleted, and Modified states.
Identify a newly attached entity as initially represented by the Detached or Unchanged state according to how it enters the context.
Explain that Add marks a new entity for insertion when changes are saved.
Explain that Update is one of the explicit methods that attaches or tracks an entity for update processing.
Identify disposal of a DbContext as one event that stops its entities from being tracked by that context.
Explain that querying, modifying an entity, and calling SaveChanges is a standard EF Core unit-of-work pattern.
Distinguish ExecuteUpdate from a sequence that loads entities, changes them in memory, and then calls SaveChanges.
Explain that ExecuteDelete is an EF Core bulk operation for deleting matching database rows without first loading each entity.
Identify ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete as operations that execute immediately against the database rather than being accumulated in the change tracker.
Explain that a foreign key represents the dependent-side link in a relationship between entity types.
Identify navigation properties as .NET properties used to navigate between related entity instances.
Distinguish the principal and dependent ends of a relationship in an EF Core model.
Explain that EF Core relationships may be configured by convention or explicitly through model configuration.
Identify a one-to-many relationship as one principal related to zero or more dependent entities.
Explain that a one-to-one relationship connects one principal entity with at most one dependent entity on the other side.
Identify a many-to-many relationship as a relationship in which multiple entities on each side can be related.
Explain that EF Core can discover related entity types by recursively exploring navigation properties.
Identify a model snapshot as the previous-model representation used when calculating migration differences.
Explain that migration source files can be committed to source control like other project source files.
Identify adding a migration as a design-time operation performed with EF Core tools after a model change.
Explain that updating a database applies migrations to create or evolve its schema.
Distinguish migration files that describe changes from the database schema that receives those changes.
Identify EF Core tools as primarily intended for design-time development tasks.
Distinguish the Visual Studio Package Manager Console tools from the cross-platform .NET CLI tools.
Explain reverse engineering as generating a DbContext and entity types from an existing database schema.
Diagnose sharing a single DbContext concurrently across threads as an unsupported usage pattern.
Explain why every asynchronous EF Core operation should be awaited before another operation starts on the same context.
Identify the normal ASP.NET Core request-scoped registration behavior of AddDbContext.
objectives.citation: DbContext in dependency injection for ASP.NET Core

objectives.statement: Distinguish a DbContext factory as a way to create context instances when the normal request scope is not sufficient.
Explain that provider translation means the same LINQ expression can be translated into provider-specific query language.
Identify database execution as occurring when an EF Core query is materialized or otherwise executed against the provider.
Explain why no-tracking queries avoid the overhead of maintaining entity state when changes will not be saved.
Distinguish identity resolution from change tracking: the former can reuse instances while the latter records changes for persistence.
Explain that a custom projection may still track entity instances contained in its result when the query is tracking.
Identify the model snapshot and current model comparison as the basis for detecting schema changes in migrations.
Explain that migrations are designed to update a schema incrementally rather than recreate it for every model change.
Distinguish model configuration precedence where explicit Fluent API configuration overrides convention-based configuration.
Explain that an entity type can be excluded from migrations while remaining part of the EF Core model.
Identify source control as an appropriate place to track generated migration source files for a project.
Explain how EF Core uses a metadata model to map entity types to an underlying database.
Identify OnModelCreating as the method commonly used to apply Fluent API model configuration.
Explain how a provider-specific configuration can supplement general EF Core model configuration.
Distinguish a DbSet property from a physical table: the property exposes an entity set in the model while mapping is configured separately.
Identify table name and table schema as relational mapping choices for an entity type.
Explain that EF Core can map an entity type to a database view rather than a normal table.
Identify the context's DbSet properties and OnModelCreating as two ways entity types can enter the model.
Explain that a provider may ignore configuration that it does not support or that is not applicable to its data store.
Distinguish loading a single entity from loading all entities in the standard EF Core query patterns.
Explain that a LINQ query can be composed with filtering before it is sent to the database.
Identify the default tracking behavior as applying to entity types with a key, while keyless entity types are never tracked.
Explain how configuring the default tracking behavior changes the baseline for context queries.
Distinguish a tracked query result from a no-tracking result when deciding whether later changes can be persisted by SaveChanges.
Identify the change tracker as a source of current and original values used to detect modifications.
Explain that disposing a context ends its unit of work and releases the tracking scope for its entities.
Distinguish direct bulk operations from entity-instance updates when choosing between ExecuteUpdate and SaveChanges.
Explain that migration generation compares model metadata rather than merely comparing database table text.
Identify reverse engineering as a tooling workflow rather than the normal runtime query workflow.
Diagnose starting parallel operations on one context as a lifetime and threading design error rather than a query translation feature.
Explain how a short-lived context, awaited operations, and SaveChanges define a safe unit-of-work pattern.
objectives.citation: The DbContext lifetime; Asynchronous operation pitfalls; Approach 1: change tracking and SaveChanges
